Chapter 2: Observations

Summary:

Another summary

Chapter Text

The afternoon light moved slowly across the room. Somewhere beyond the window, a train was passing, its low sound briefly filling the spaces between their words. She set her notebook on the desk and watched the shadows shift.

It was an ordinary observation, the kind that rarely makes it into a written account. And yet there was something in the stillness that seemed to deserve attention: the small distance between an expectation and the thing itself.

“Perhaps we should begin again,” he said. She turned back to the first page. There were annotations in the margins and a sentence underlined twice. Nothing had been erased; nothing had been settled.

The city continued outside. Beneath the window, footsteps passed and faded. They had all the time they needed, or at least enough to consider the question carefully.

By the following morning, the pattern had become clearer. Each return to the same place revealed a different detail, as though the room itself were changing in response to the attention it received.

Chapter is a word in the story and must not be changed. [1]
